answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The saffron multiplier is published, charged in kernel, and canyon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 3467 identities would post 3410 proofs and burn roughly 89 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
